questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A farmer is able to grow three crops, X, Y and Z, on his land. The farmer decides to grow at most two crops in any year. The table shows six possible combinations of units of output of the three crops. output X 0 0 80 40 40 0 Y 0 60 0 30 0 30 Z 40 0 0 0 20 20 What is the opportunity cost of 1 unit of X?

options.A: 1.33 units of Y
options.D: 2.0 units of Z

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a production possibility curve for an economy that produces capital goods and consumer goods. capital goods O consumer goods Why is the production possibility curve drawn concave to the origin?

options.A: Capital goods are a more labour intensive output than consumer goods.
options.B: Consumers always seek to maximise their satisfaction from consumption.
options.C: Profit maximisation for firms always ensures efficiency in production.
options.D: Some resources are more efficient in production of some goods than others.

questions.questionText: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is a branch of the United States Government which regulates markets. What does its name imply is most likely to be its main responsibility?

options.A: to prevent harm from demerit goods
options.B: to provide subsidies for essential goods
options.C: to raise revenue from goods in elastic demand
options.D: to safeguard employment in manufacturing industry

questions.questionText: What is treated as a variable in constructing a market demand curve?

options.A: consumers’ tastes
options.D: the price of the good

questions.questionText: The diagram shows how the quantity demanded of four goods changes as income changes. Which good has an income elasticity of demand which is always +1?

options.A: B C quantity of good demanded D O income

questions.questionText: The table shows three different prices and quantities supplied per week of two products, X and Y. price of X quantity price of Y quantity ($) supplied of X ($) supplied of Y
110 50 80 Which statement about price elasticity of supply (PES) is correct?

options.A: The PES of X is elastic for a fall in its price from $15 to $10.
options.B: The PES of X is unitary for a rise in its price from $15 to $20.
options.C: The PES of Y is elastic for a fall in its price from $40 to $30.
options.D: The PES of Y is unitary for a rise in its price from $40 to $50.

questions.questionText: In 2016 car drivers bought more fuel (gas) because the price of oil from which it was made had fallen. Which diagram represents this change in the market for fuel?

options.A: B price price S of fuel of fuel S D
options.D: 2 D

questions.questionText: The market demand for a product is made up of the demand from three firms, X, Y and Z. The table shows the demand from each firm and the market supply. price $ demand from X demand from Y demand from Z market supply
Good X has a substitute, good Y, and a complement, good Z. The price of good Y decreases and the price of good Z increases. Why might the equilibrium price of good X remain unchanged?

options.A: Producers of good X adopt new technology.
options.B: Producers of good X receive a subsidy.
options.C: Some firms stop production of good X.
options.D: The tax on the production of good X is cut.

questions.questionText: At first, a television service is available at no charge. The television company then charges viewers $6 per hour to watch its programmes. The demand curve is D. price ($) D 0 2000 5000 number of hours viewed What is the value of the loss in consumer surplus and what value of consumer surplus remains after the introduction of the hourly charge? lost consumer remaining consumer surplus ($) surplus ($)

Which benefit is most likely to result from a rise in the minimum price of labour (wage rate)?

options.A: a reduction in costs of production
options.C: a reduction in the level of unemployment
options.D: a reduction in the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: The table shows the demand and supply schedules for a product before and after the government pays a subsidy of $4 per unit to the producers. quantity quantity supplied quantity supplied price demanded before subsidy after subsidy $ (units) (units) (units)
Which statement about transfer payments is correct?

options.A: Transfer payments are intended to reward productive economic activity.
options.B: Transfer payments are only financed by government.
options.C: Transfer payments may result in a disincentive to work.
options.D: Transfer payments will include the sales of new cars.

questions.questionText: What is the major problem associated with a government directly providing the correct amount of a public good?

options.A: competition from private producers
options.D: rivalry in consumption

questions.questionText: An aggregate demand curve slopes downwards from left to right. One reason for this is that a reduction in the average price level will lead to

options.A: a decline in the country’s international competitiveness.
options.C: an increase in the real value of money balances.
options.D: the expectation of further price falls.

questions.questionText: During one year the national output of a country valued in terms of money prices increased by 8% while the index of the prices of all goods and services produced in the country increased by 3%. By how much did the real national output increase?

The table shows the CPI rate of inflation (%) in the United States from 2006 to 2013. 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2.5% 4.1% 0.1% 2.7% 1.5% 3.0% 1.7% 2.0% What can be concluded from the figures about the period 2006 to 2013?

options.A: There was one year of constant prices.
options.B: There were three years of deflation.
options.C: There were only four years of inflation.
options.D: There were eight years of rising living costs.

questions.questionText: In 2014 Australia and China negotiated a trade agreement. This removed Chinese tariffs on 95% of Australian exports in exchange for greater access to the Australian economy for Chinese investors. How would the agreement be expected to affect the Australian balance of payments in the short run? current account financial account

options.A: greater inflow greater inflow
options.D: greater outflow greater outflow

questions.questionText: Turkey can produce a good but also imports some of the good from Egypt. The Turkish currency depreciates against the Egyptian currency. How is this most likely to affect production of this good in Egypt and in Turkey? production in Egypt production in Turkey

options.A: decrease decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: The table shows the terms of trade for Saudi Arabia. date terms of trade 2000 100 2010 105 2015 137 What can be concluded from the table for Saudi Arabia?

options.A: Export prices rose relative to import prices.
options.B: The balance of trade surplus increased.
options.C: The volume of exports exceeded the volume of imports.
options.D: The volume of exports rose faster than the volume of imports.

questions.questionText: What is present in a customs union but not in a free trade area?

options.A: a common external tariff with the rest of the world
options.D: the free movement of all goods, services and factors of production

questions.questionText: Which argument in favour of protectionism is not generally regarded as economically valid?

options.A: It increases the standard of living of the population in general.
options.B: It prevents heavily-subsidised imports from competing unfairly against domestic goods.
options.C: It provides time for the protected industry’s workers to be retrained for other work.
options.D: Once the protected industry becomes established, it will produce efficiently.

questions.questionText: Which action is classified as a fiscal policy measure?

options.A: fixing a currency to another country’s currency
options.B: managing changes in the level of government debt
options.C: providing guidance to industry and the public
options.D: tightening reserve asset requirements for financial institutions

questions.questionText: A country has a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments. Which policy would be expected to increase the deficit?

options.A: an appreciation of the exchange rate
options.D: a rise in subsidies to domestic firms

questions.questionText: Which type of policy would have the most immediate effect in dealing with a deflationary economic downturn?

options.A: increasing the government’s budget surplus
options.B: increasing liquidity by assisting banks to lend more
options.C: investing in projects to improve transport networks
